rci3_hc_age.reason:
Table 1 provides Age (mean ± std) for Healthy controls in Discovery (34 ± 9.5), Replication 1 (34 ± 11.3), and Replication 2 (30 ± 8.0). 
To calculate the overall mean and pooled standard deviation, a weighted average was used.
Overall Mean = (256 * 34 + 400 * 34 + 312 * 30) / (256 + 400 + 312) = 31664 / 968 = 32.71.
Pooled Standard Deviation was calculated using the formula: SD = sqrt(Total SS / Total df) where Total SS = sum( (n_i-1)*sd_i^2 + n_i*(mean_i - OverallMean)^2 ) and Total df = sum(n_i) - 1. This resulted in SD = 10.03.
The age range (min-max) is not reported in the table.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: CAT12; SPM12; VBM-SPM12; segmentation; normalization; bias-field correction; 8 mm FWHM Gaussian smoothing; gray matter mask
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The 'Estimation of gray matter volume' section explicitly lists the software, versions, and processing steps.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: raw T1-weighted MRI volumes were processed using the computational analysis toolbox version 12 (CAT12; http://www.neuro.uni-jena.de/software/), based on statistical parametric mapping version 12 (SPM12). Images were segmented, normalized, and bias-field-corrected using VBM-SPM12 (http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm, London, UK) (Ashburner and Friston, 2000, 2003), yielding images containing gray and white matter segments. Prior to the estimation of the normative models, all gray and white matter volumes were smoothed with an 8 mm FWHM Gaussian smoothing kernel and we restricted our analyses to voxels included in the gray matter mask constructed for the discovery study.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Nonparametric test (Bonferroni-Holm correction) for associations between diagnosis and deviation scores; Mann-Whitney U test for group comparisons of percentages of extreme deviations; Pearson correlations for associations between extreme deviations and PANSS scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Group-level differences in brain structure between patients and healthy individuals were robustly replicated, but these differences disguise considerable individual-level heterogeneity in brain structural aberrations.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Normative models performed well across the brain. Robust group-level differences were replicated between patients and healthy individuals, with schizophrenia patients showing a significantly higher percentage of extreme negative deviations (e.g., Rep1: 0.64±1.15% vs healthy: 0.16±0.44%), being 3.91-4.95 times more prevalent in schizophrenia than healthy controls. Conversely, healthy individuals showed a higher percentage of extreme positive deviations compared to both patient groups. Extreme negative deviations correlated significantly with PANSS scores across all samples. While group differences were robust, individual-level neuroanatomical distributions of extreme deviations were highly heterogeneous, with sparse overlap across individuals within the same diagnosis (peak overlap for schizophrenia ~9.5%). These findings were consistent across various Z-thresholds and when using extreme value statistics. Sex stratification indicated stronger overlap of negative deviations in males for both disorders.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Other data modalities might be more effective in capturing common pathophysiological processes; potential for misinterpretation due to scanning confounds when replicating across multiple scanners and sequences; study was conducted on a predominantly adult sample, limiting generalizability to adolescence/early adulthood; weaker replication of bipolar disorder findings in cerebellum due to smaller sample sizes.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: it must be considered that other data modalities beyond those provided by structural brain imaging may be more able to capture any common pathophysiological processes...; Note here, that if you replicate these findings in a sample on multiple scanners using different scanning sequences your interpretation might be misguided due to scanning confounds.; we worked on a predominantly adult sample, however, the onset of schizophrenia is primarily in adolescence or early adulthood.; for bipolar disorder the replication is not as strong showing differences from healthy controls in the cerebellum only in the discovery sample but not in the two replication samples. This may be due to a lower sample size of the bipolar and schizophrenia groups in both replication samples.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Analytical pipeline made publicly available for replication and application to other cohorts/disorders; plans to scale up work to larger samples, wider age ranges (neurodevelopment), incorporate different modalities (e.g., brain network level, genetics), and link different experimental designs to normative modeling.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is a replication study of previous findings by Wolfers et al. (2018). The analytical pipeline used in the study has been made publicly available.
